[USER] User inquired about an overview of various weapon systems and armaments deployed by modern naval vessels and their use in combat.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Modern naval vessels feature a variety of weapons systems and armaments designed for specific tactical roles.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Large caliber guns are found on the largest naval vessels, such as battleships or aircraft carriers, firing large, high-explosive shells over long distances.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Missiles are the primary offensive weapon of modern naval vessels, available in anti-ship, anti-aircraft, and land-attack variants.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Torpedoes are underwater missiles launched from submarines, torpedo boats, or surface ships, used to attack other ships or underwater targets.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Close-in weapons systems (CIWS) are rapid-fire machine guns or cannons designed to engage incoming missiles or aircraft at close range, often mounted on a rotating turret with automated targeting.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Anti-submarine weapons include depth charges, sonar systems, and torpedoes, designed to detect and destroy underwater threats, particularly submarines.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Electronic warfare (EW) systems disrupt or jam enemy communications and radar systems and can counter enemy missiles by spoofing their guidance systems.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] In combat, naval vessels use a combination of these weapons systems to engage enemy targets, employing long-range missiles, guns for closer engagements, and CIWS for defense against incoming threats.  
[USER] User expressed interest in whether different countries have different preferences for naval armaments or if it is standardized worldwide.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Different countries have varying naval armament preferences based on strategic needs, budget, and resources.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Countries with large coastlines may invest heavily in battleships and aircraft carriers, while others may prioritize submarines and missile technology.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Some countries develop their own weapons systems, such as Russia's Kalibr missiles and China's DF-21D "carrier killer" missile.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Certain weapon systems like missiles and torpedo defenses are commonly found on most modern naval vessels worldwide, but specific armament varies by country.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Major advancements in naval armaments are expected in the future, with potential developments in several areas.
